items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We did a concert at Town Hall with a big band. We had rehearsed, and he had a lot of new music

ctx.x: You did some work with Mingus outside of the band. One of them is a situation in Town Hall.

Oh yeah. We did a concert at Town Hall with a big band. We had rehearsed, and he had a lot of new music, but he brought it all too late, and it was impossible for the music to have been played in the short period of time that we had to rehearse it in. He was just going to bulldoze the date anyhow, which he did. So he had us come in tuxedos for the concert at Town Hall, and he was a little late showing up. We’re on the bandstand. Finally he shows up with a tank shirt on – a tee shirt, rather, and a sloppy cap…

I understand that at the – somehow at the end of this concert, that he walked off and they were bringing the curtain down, and you started playing In a Mellotone or something like that, trying maybe to further salvage the evening?

items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I asked Duke, when are we going to make that record, Clark Terry, Dan Jones, myself and you

ctx.x: What are some of the other -- that's interesting, about being able to play in and out, and being an actor. Who are some of the people most able to do that? You mentioned Bird and --
I have to tell you about what Duke has done. Like, I asked Duke, when are we going to make that record, Clark Terry, Dan Jones, myself and you and some you want, to make a real avant garde record?
